subject.title: [Bug]: /context detail shows ~62k untracked provider/runtime overhead on fresh OpenAI Codex gpt-5.5 session

question: Should `/context detail` grow a provider-aware Codex context ledger, and which buckets should count toward user-facing context and compaction warnings?
rationale: The code path is clear, but OpenClaw needs maintainer intent and live Codex evidence before assigning billing, cache, native-thread, and unknown residual meanings to user-visible context buckets.

options.title: Define ledger after live Codex proof
options.body: Run a fresh Codex OAuth reproduction, then add explicit measured/inferred/unknown buckets and keep compaction semantics tied only to buckets that truly occupy the context window.

options.title: Keep generic overhead wording
options.body: Leave `/context detail` as a rough tracked-versus-reported comparison and avoid changing compaction behavior until a stronger provider contract exists.

options.title: Document the limitation only
options.body: Add docs or inline wording that the residual is unexplained provider/runtime usage without adding new bucket logic yet.

recommendation.title: Define ledger after live Codex proof
recommendation.body: Run a fresh Codex OAuth reproduction, then add explicit measured/inferred/unknown buckets and keep compaction semantics tied only to buckets that truly occupy the context window.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership signal on the same context diagnostics surface and related compactability cleanup makes this the best available routing candidate.
